case_name: R.S. Makashi & Ors. v I.M. Menon & Ors.
facts: The second world war left in its wake conditions of scarcity of foodgrains and other essential commodities in different parts of the country.

To tide over that situation and with intent to ensure a fair and equitable distribution of the available supply of foodgrains etc., schemes of rationing of foodgrains were periodically introduced in the different States in the country.

In November, 1957 an informal (non-statutory) scheme of rationing was introduced in the State of Bombay and for administering the said scheme, an ad hoc Organisation was set up under the Controller of Foodgrains Distribution.

The CFD was manned principally by personnel who had been working in the temporary Civil Supplies Department created during the second world war period and who were attending to certain residual duties concerned with the winding up of that department, persons taken on deputation from other Government departments, retrenched former Civil Supply Department personnel, and persons directly recruited to the CFD by the Controller of Foodgrains Distribution on temporary basis through the Employment Exchange.

Since no rules had been framed laying down the qualifications or method of recruitment to the various posts, the guiding factor which seems to have weighed with the authorities in effecting appointments in the CFD was the suitability of the person concerned to carry out the duties attached to a particular post irrespective of qualifications, age, etc.
The principles to be observed for fixing the seniority of the personnel appointed to the CFD were laid down by the State Government by a Resolution dated April 1, 1963.
In July 1965, the Government of India issued instructions to all the State Governments advising them to start statutory rationing schemes in metropolitan areas and big towns.

With a view to implement those instructions of the Central Government, the State Government of Maharashtra sanctioned on October 21, 1965 a skeleton staff for working out details and carrying out other preliminary work for the introduction of a scheme of statutory rationing in Greater Bombay.

Subsequently, by a Resolution dated February 11, 1966, the Government of Maharashtra announced its decision to introduce a statutory rationing scheme in Bombay and the Industrial Complex around it including some areas of Thana District and to set up an organisation under the Controller of Rationing, Bombay, for efficiently administering the said statutory scheme.

The strength and pattern of the staff for the Bombay Rationing Organisation (for short, the BRO) which was newly created under the said Resolution was to be as shown in Annexure 'A' appended to the Resolution.
Out of these, 1220 newly created posts were in the category of Rationing Inspectors and 165 posts were of Senior Clerks.

In compliance with the directions contained in the said letter, a large number of personnel from different departments of the State Government of Maharashtra in the Greater Bombay area were sent over to the BRO on deputation and they were appointed to posts in different categories in the new Organisation (B.R.O.)

As an essential preliminary step for the integration of the former CFD personnel with the staff appointed in the BRO from other sources, the Controller of Rationing, Bombay published on 29.8.1966 a provisional Gradation List of the CFD personnel as on March 1, 1966.

Subsequently, on March 22, 1968, the Government of Maharashtra issued the 'Bombay Rationing Organisation (Fixation of Seniority) Rules, 1968', laying down the principles to be applied for the fixation of seniority of the persons working in the BRO.
issues: What are the principles to be observed for fixing the seniority of the personnel appointed to the CFD?
How should the seniority of a released Government Servant and a Merged Government Servant in the cadre of Senior Clerk, Rationing Inspector and Deputy Accountants be determined?
What is the procedure for fixation of seniority of persons in the cadre of Senior Clerks/Rationing Inspectors/Deputy Accountants?
court_reasoning: The principles to be observed for fixing the seniority of the personnel appointed to the CFD were laid down by the State Government by a Resolution dated April 1, 1963.

The seniority of a released Government Servant and a Merged Government Servant in the cadre of Senior Clerk, Rationing Inspector and Deputy Accountants shall be determined with reference to dates which shall be fixed after deducting two years from the length of continuous service, whether officiating or permanent rendered by him in the cadre of clerks, typists, and clerk-cum-typist.

The seniority amongst them will be fixed as under: Provided that in the case of merged Government servant who was recruited to the post of Supply Inspector or Senior Clerk, by nomination, he shall take rank above a clerk in the former Foodgrains Distribution Scheme who was promoted to the cadre of Supply Inspector or Senior Clerk, in the former Foodgrains Distribution Scheme immediately after him and if this be not the position, above the first person in the cadre of clerks belonging to that organisation who is posted in the cadre of Senior Clerks, Rationing Inspectors and Deputy Accountants on and after 1st March 1966.
